newsitem.title: USA: DOT to hold hearing on Miami airport fees.
newsitem.headline: DOT to hold hearing on Miami airport fees.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Transportation announced Wednesday it will hold hearings on a request by Miami's Dade County to determine the reasonableness of fees it charges airlines at Miami International Airport.

This is part of a controversy caused by AMR Corp's American Airlines new terminal at the airport. Other airlines have claimed that they are being asked to foot the bill for Amrerican's building with the increased fees.
Several airlines sued Dade County and a U.S. District Court judge ruled that the DOT should make a determination.
No date or location has been set for DOT the hearing, but it will likely be announced in a few days, a DOT spokesman said.
It is the first time an airport has requested such a determination, DOT said.
"We are very happy with the proceedings. We consider this a victory," said an airport spokesman.

The airport boosted some fees on October 1. Landing fees jumped to $1.34 per 1,000 pounds of aircraft from $1.15. That means a 757 passenger plane costs $268 to land, up from $230. For a carrier with a daily 757 flight, that amounts to $14,000 per year, an airport official said.
A 747 freighter costs $844 to land, up from $724, or $18,000 a year more for the typical three times per week flight, he said.
Dade County also increased terminal rents.

The case will be heard by a DOT administrative law judge who must issue a decision by Feb. 17, 1997, according to the announcement. DOT will review the judge's decision and issue its final decion by March 19, 1997.
On Nov. 19 the County asked DOT to determine if its new fees were reasonable.

Six airlines -- Air Canada, Delta Air Lines Inc, Deutsche Lufthansa AG, Trans World Airlines Corp, UAL Corp's United Airlines and USAir Group Inc -- filed an answer to the airport's request arguing that the increases are unreasonable and unfair, DOT's announcement said.
The fee dispute involves Dade County's allocation of the cost of the airport's expansion and reconstruction for terminal space to be used by American Airlines, the announcement said.
The county contends that its fees are fair and based on the airport's established fee methodology.
The airlines argue that the county is unfairly charging them for part of the cost of the new American Airlines facilities, the announcement said.
